ABSTRACT: A distinctive N-substituent-controlled regioselective 1,4-hydrocarbona-
tion or 1,4-hydrocarbonation/5-endo-trig cyclization cascade reaction of β-CF
3
-1,3-
enynamides with β-dicarbonyl compounds in the presence of a simple base is reported.
β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides having a Ts group N-substituent produce γ-CF
3
-allenamides via
a 1,4-hydrocarbonation process, whereas β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides bearing a Ms group N-
substituent lead to 3-CF
3
-cyclopentenylamines through a 1,4-hydrocarbonation/5-endo-
trig cyclization cascade process.
A
llenamides
1
and cyclopentenylamines
2
are two types of
important structural motifs of natural products and
pharmaceutically relevant molecules (Figure 1). The allena-
mide motifs are also recognized as flexible synthetic building
blocks in diverse synthetic conversions and are outstanding
precursors for the synthesis of natural products.
3
Conse-
quently, the synthesis of these two versatile units has garnered
extensive research interest, leading to a range of strategies for
their functionalized construction.
4,5
On the other hand,
building blocks incorporating CF
3
are regarded as essential
structural motifs in the fields of medicinal chemistry and
agrochemistry.
6
Due to the distinctive reactivity of allenes
7
and
their capacity to participate in various transformations to create
valuable complex structures,
8
trifluoromethyl-allenes have
attracted significant attention regarding their synthetic method.
As a consequence, substantial efforts have been made over the
years by synthetic organic chemists to design and develop
methods allowing efficient access to a variety of functionalized
CF
3
-allenes.
9
Despite the impressive achievements in CF
3
-
allenes synthesis, however, less attention has been paid to the
development of new synthetic methods for the synthesis of
trifluoromethylated allenamides. In 2016, Evano and Blanchard
first reported the synthesis of γ-trifluoromethylated allena-

mides from protected trifluoromethylated propargylic amines
via base-induced isomerization (Scheme 1a). The exploration
of the reactivity of γ-trifluoromethylated allenamides demon-
strated that they serve as outstanding substrates for cyclizations
catalyzed by radicals and gold(I), leading to the formation of
fluoroalkylated nitrogen heterocycles.
10
In 2022, Miesch’s
group reported an elegant copper-catalyzed coupling of
ynamides and fluorinated diazoalkanes, enabling fluorine-
substituted N-allenamides to be obtained (Scheme 1b).
11
Among them, CF
3
-N-allenamides are useful building blocks for
the preparation of functionalized stereodefined difluorinated
dienes, monofluorinated dienes,
12
and γ-sultams.
13
Very
recently, we developed a new metal-free method for the
efficient preparation of 3-trifluoromethyl pyrroles through
highly regioselective 1,4-hydroamination/cyclization/aromati-
zation cascade reactions of β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides with alkyl
primary amines. Evidence for the highly regioselective 1,4-
hydroamination was observed after the isolation and character-
ization of the allenamide intermediate (Scheme 1c).
14
As a
continuation of our interest in the synthesis of fluorinated
carbocycles and heterocycles
15
and the chemistry of β-CF
3
-1,3-
enynamides, we were intrigued by the possibility of extending
this annulation method to include 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds.
It is well-known that the electronic properties and the
reactivity of allenamides can be tuned by the selection of the
N-substituent group.
3b
We envisioned that functionalized γ-
CF
3
-allenamide intermediate 3 would be formed in the same
way through regioselective 1,4-hydrocarbonation of β-CF
3
-1,3-
enynamide 1 with β-dicarbonyl compound 2 under a proper
choice of a base. Unlike our previous reports,
14
this γ-CF
3
-
allenamide intermediate 3 may be stable and separable or
undergo further intramolecular 5-endo-trig cyclization to give 3-
CF
3
-cyclopentenylamines 4, depending on the N-substituent
group. Herein, we are pleased to report our recent results on
this simple base-mediated divergent reaction of β-CF
3
-1,3-
enynamides with β-dicarbonyl compounds leading to γ-CF
3
-
allenamides or 3-CF
3
-cyclopentenylamines, and the reactions
are substrate-dependent (Scheme 1d).
To test our assumption, 4-methyl-N-propyl-N-(3-
(trifluoromethyl)but-3-en-1-yn-1-yl)benzenesulfonamide 1a
and dimethyl malonate 2a were selected as model substrates
for reaction screening. Initially, 1a and 2a (1.5 equiv) were
subjected to the reaction in CH
3
CN at room temperature with
Na
2
CO
3
(1.5 equiv) as a base; however, after 24 h, no reaction
occurred according to TLC analysis (Table 1, entry 1). To our
delight, when the reaction was performed at 60 °C, the
expected functionalized γ-CF
3
-allenamides 3a was indeed
formed, albeit in 33% yield without full consumption of
material 1a (Table 1, entry 2). To speed up the reaction, an
elevated temperature (80 °C) was used; however, the reaction

became complicated, indicating the allenamide product was
not stable at high temperature (Table 1, entry 3). To further
improve the yield of 3a, we turned our attention to screening
the base and solvent, and Cs
2
CO
3
gave a similar result as
Na
2
CO
3
in terms of yield and conversion (Table 1, entry 4);
however, organic bases such as Et
3
N and DMAP gave no
reaction (Table 1, entries 5 and 6). Among the solvents tested,
THF was found to be optimal (Table 1, entries 7 and 8).
Moreover, by increasing the ratio of malonate 2a to β-CF
3
-1,3-
enynamide 1a, the yield was further improved (Table 1, entry
9). After numerous attempts, we were pleased to find that the
desired γ-CF
3
-allenamide 3a product was isolated in 78% yield
when the reaction was run at an increased concentration
(Table 1, entry 10), and the reaction conditions were thus
defined as the standard reaction conditions for subsequent
investigations.
With suitable reaction conditions established (Table 1, entry
10), we next explored the scope and limitations of the process
with respect to the β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides bearing a Ts N-
substituent group and β-dicarbonyl compounds, and the results
are summarized in Scheme 2. First, the reaction can be scaled
up to 1 mmol without a loss of efficiency. In general, a series of
malonate derivatives, β-diketones, and β-ketoesters could be
employed as reaction partners to afford the corresponding
functionalized γ-CF
3
-allenamides in moderate to good yields
(3a−3f). In the case of malonate, the steric effect of the
substitution on the ester group could not be negligible; for
example, changing the ester group from methyl to isopropyl or
benzyl showed an obvious difference in terms of yield (3a−
3d). When the unsymmetrical β-dicarbonyl compounds such
as β-keto esters were subjected to the reaction, the desired
allenamide 3f was obtained as a mixture of two diastereomers
in good yields but with poor diastereoselectivity (1:1.4). With
respect to the β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides with a Ts N-substituent
group, substituents linked to the nitrogen atom also have
dramatic effects on the outcome of the reaction. For example,
switching n-propyl to a methyl group, the reaction became
complicated, some unidentified compounds were formed, and
allenamide 3g was only obtained in 34% isolated yield.
However, benzyl was tolerated for this transformation,
producing allenamide 3h in 88% isolated yield. β-CF
3
-1,3-
Enynamides 1 with Ts N-substituent groups bearing different
aryl groups such as phenyl and substituted phenyl linked to the
nitrogen atom are quite general substrates for the synthesis of
γ-CF
3
-allenamides (3i−3k).
In the course of studying the reactivity of β-CF
3
-1,3-
enynamides 1 through the selection of different electron-
withdrawing groups attached to the nitrogen atom, we found it
very interesting that under similar reaction conditions the
replacement of the Ts group in β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides 1 with a
Ms group switches the reaction outcome, and cyclopentenyl-
amine formed via double hydrocarbonation sequence was
observed (Scheme 3). For example, treatment of N-propyl-N-
(3-(trifluoromethyl)but-3-en-1-yn-1-yl)methanesulfonamide
1h with dimethyl malonate 2a under similar reaction
conditions for γ-CF
3
-allenamide synthesis delivers cyclo-
pentenylamine 4a in 73% isolated yield. The structure of 4a
was further confirmed by single-crystal X-ray analysis.
16
We
think that allenamide intermediates with Ms groups formed via
the first intermolecular hydrocarbonation have less steric
effects and thus are prone to the second intramolecular
hydrocarbonation to give the cyclopentenylamine product.
The scope of β-dicarbonyl compounds was then examined, and
the results are summarized in Scheme 3. Similar to that for γ-
CF
3
-allenamide formation, a series of malonate derivatives, β-
diketones, β-ketoesters, and N,N-dimethylbarbituric acid are
quite general substrates for cyclopentenylamine synthesis (4a−
4i). Similarly, when the unsymmetrical β-dicarbonyl com-
pounds such as unsymmetrical 1,3-diketones or β-ketoesters
were subjected to the reaction, the desired cyclopentenyl-
amines were obtained as a mixture of two diastereomers in
good yields with good diastereoselectivity (4g, 4h). β-CF
3
-1,3-
Enynamides 1 with a Ms N-substituent group bearing other
alkyl group such as benzyl or an aryl such as phenyl linked to
the nitrogen atom are also quite general substrates for
cyclopentenylamine synthesis (4j, 4k).
The scope of the β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides 1 with other
electron-withdrawing groups such as Ac and Boc was also
investigated using dimethyl malonate 2a as the reaction
partner. β-CF
3
-1,3-Enynamides with an Ac N-substituent
group failed to give any detected products, and the reaction
became very complicated; however, the reaction of β-CF
3
-1,3-
enynamides with a Boc N-substituent group needs an elevated
temperature and affords inseparable double bond isomer
mixture of cyclopentenylamine 5 in 73% isolated yield (eq 1).
Interestingly, β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides with a Ts N-substituent
group bearing cyclopentyl linked to the nitrogen atom affords
gem-difluorinated ene−ynamides 6 through an S
N
2′ reaction
process
17
in 70% isolated yield; however, replacement of the
Ts group with Ms group switches the reaction outcome, and
functionalized γ-CF
3
-allenamide 7 is formed (eq 2). Besides β-
dicarbonyl compounds, active methylene compounds such as
malonitrile were also investigated. β-CF
3
-1,3-Enynamides with
a Ts or Ms N-substituent group bearing n-propyl linked to the
nitrogen atom both fail to undergo a clean reaction with
malonitrile. β-CF
3
-1,3-Enynamides with the Ms N-substituent
group failed to give any detected products; through
replacement of the Ms group with the Ts group, cyclo-
pentenylamine 8 could be obtained, albeit in low yield (eq 3).
These results clearly demonstrated that both substituents on
the nitrogen atom of β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides and nucleophiles
had a dramatic effect on the reaction diversity.A plausible
mechanism for the divergent formation of allenamides,
cyclopentenylamine, and gem-difluorinated ene−ynamides is
proposed in Scheme 4. The regioselective nucleophilic
addition of the anion intermediate A to β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamide
1 would afford two resonance-stabilized anions, allenamide
carbanion intermediate B or propargylic anion intermediate C
(α-trifluoromethyl carbanion), depending on the N-substituent
group effects of enynamide 1 and nucleophiles. The stabilized
allenamide carbanion would facilitate allenamide 3 formation.
If allenamide 3 contained suitable electronic and steric factors,
it would further undergo an intramolecular nucleophilic
addition under basic reaction conditions to give the cyclo-
pentene carbanion intermediate D. The protonation of
intermediate D would produce the final product cyclopentenyl-
amine 4. On the other hand, if an α-trifluoromethyl carbanion
is prone to form, it would undergo defluorination to give gem-
difluorinated ene−ynamide 6 via an E
1
cb reaction process. An
alternative reaction pathway for gem-difluorinated ene−
ynamide 6 formation from allenamide carbanion intermediate
B through δ-extrusion of fluorine was also plausible.
12
To demonstrate the synthetic practicability of this method-
ology, further transformations representative of γ-CF
3
-
allenamides 3a and 3e and cyclopentenylamine 4a were
performed (Scheme 5). A Pd-catalyzed
18
or NIS-mediated
19

13792

cycloisomerization of γ-CF
3
-allenamide 3a furnished the
cyclopentenylamine 9 and an inseparable double bond isomer
mixture of iodo-substituted cyclopentenylamine 10, respec-
tively. Upon treatment of γ-CF
3
-allenamide 3e with 2.0 equiv
of TMSCl in THF at 0 °C, the trifluoromethyl-substituted 2,5-
dihydrooxepine 11 could be obtained in 78% isolated yield. In
addition, one ester group at the ring position of cyclopentenyl-
amine 4a could be hydrolyzed under acidic reaction conditions
by treatment of 4a with HBr-HOAc at 60 °C, affording
cyclopentenylamine 12 with the Ms group intact. Decarbox-
ylation of 12 could be realized under basic reaction conditions
to give cyclopentenylamine 13 in 52% yield.
In conclusion, a simple base-mediated 1,4-hydrocarbonation
or 1,4-hydrocarbonation/5-endo-trig cyclization cascade reac-
tion of β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides with β-dicarbonyl compounds
affording γ-CF
3
-allenamides or cyclopentenylamines has been
developed. The reaction is substrate-dependent. In general, β-
CF
3
-1,3-enynamides having a Ts group N-substituent produce
γ-CF
3
-allenamides via a 1,4-hydrocarbonation process, whereas
β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides bearing a Ms group N-substituent lead
to 3-CF
3
-cyclopentenylamines through a 1,4-hydrocarbona-
tion/5-endo-trig cyclization cascade process. Both substituents
on the nitrogen atom of β-CF
3
-1,3-enynamides and nucleo-
philes had a dramatic effect on the reaction diversity.
